description: NodeGoat's own-code SAST issue types (one per Snyk Code rule), each with the key fix advice a good answer should contain ('facts': any listed phrase counts). Used by tests/eval_sources.py to measure how much key advice the returned OWASP sections cover. 'held_out' entries were added after the ranking was tuned.

issues.title: Code Injection
issues.summary: Unsanitized input from the HTTP request body flows into eval, where it is executed as JavaScript code. This may result in a Code Injection vulnerability.

avoid eval / dynamic code: do not have to dynamically generate code
should only be used where necessary

issues.title: Cleartext Transmission - HTTP Instead of HTTPS
issues.summary: http.createServer uses HTTP which is an insecure protocol and should not be used in code due to cleartext transmission of information. Data in cleartext in a communication channel can be sniffed by unauthorized actors. Consider using the https module instead.

issues.title: Use of Hardcoded Passwords
issues.summary: Do not hardcode passwords in code. Found hardcoded password used in password.

issues.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
issues.summary: Expensive operation (a file system operation) is performed by an endpoint handler which does not use a rate-limiting mechanism. It may enable the attackers to perform Denial-of-service attacks. Consider using a rate-limiting middleware such as express-limit.

issues.title: Open Redirect
issues.summary: Unsanitized input from an HTTP parameter flows into redirect, where it is used as input for request redirection. This may result in an Open Redirect vulnerability.

avoid user-controlled redirects: do not allow the url as user input

issues.title: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Potentially Insecure Settings
issues.summary: The autoescape setting is set to false. Disabling it might allow for Cross-site Scripting (XSS) attacks if user input is involved.

issues.title: Information Exposure - X-Powered-By Header
issues.summary: Disable X-Powered-By header for your Express app (consider using Helmet middleware), because it exposes information about the used framework to potential attackers.

issues.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
issues.summary: Unsanitized input from an HTTP parameter flows into needle.get, where it is used as an URL to perform a request. This may result in a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability.

issues.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
issues.summary: CSRF protection is disabled for your Express app. This allows the attackers to execute requests on a user's behalf.

issues.title: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
issues.summary: Cookie misses the Secure attribute (it is false by default). Set it to true to protect the cookie from man-in-the-middle attacks.

issues.title: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
issues.summary: The method test is using a vulnerable regular expression /([0-9]+)+\#/ on the HTTP request body. This may result in a Regular expression Denial of Service attack (reDOS).

issues.title: Hardcoded Non-Cryptographic Secret
issues.summary: Avoid hardcoding values that are meant to be secret. Found a hardcoded string used in here.
